themes.title: AI M&A supercycle: every layer of the stack is consolidating
themes.summary: Stripe's ~$8bn deal to acquire OpenRouter - its largest ever - turns the payment network into the tollbooth for the AI economy. Google's expanded Marvell chip partnership, an AI-chip startup worth $6.5bn, and Nvidia funding a $20bn data-labour supplier show capital racing into every layer of silicon, talent and inference.
themes.angle: The model firm's customers are invisibly becoming Stripe's; watch where AI money is *metered*.

themes.title: GCC presses its agentic-AI & export-compute bet
themes.summary: Abu Dhabi is hedging between the US and China AI camps while pushing agentic AI into private-sector and government-wired operations; Saudi Arabia is betting on exporting computing and AI globally via DataVolt. The region's operators are embedding agentic agents into core enterprise data connectivity.
themes.angle: The Gulf's edge is not generating models but industrialising agentic-AI operations and selling compute as a national export.

themes.title: Frontier labs split on the safety question
themes.summary: OpenAI has blinked first in the safety standoff, pausing certain model work, while Anthropic insists its own measures suffice. A Reuters-reviewed study sharpens the dispute: AI makers cannot fully contain what they have released. For boards, safety posture is increasingly a competitive, regulatory and reputational variable.

themes.title: Agentic software engineering is becoming operational
themes.summary: Google claims its model can already do forward-deployed engineering work, Replit is widening software access to high-price GPT-5.6 'Luna' tier, and Bloomberg reported SpaceX approached Cognition to advance AI. Downstream cities to reduce the cost of coding-agent reliance will force salary councils to rethink the talent mix.

themes.title: Data centers become the central political liability
themes.summary: Reuters reports the GOP is telling AI companies its data centers are politically radioactive in a key Ohio Senate contest, while Axios frames rising public opposition to American data centers as the new 'existential threat' to the AI capex boom — the problem is no longer energy or China, it's the local politics of the physical engine.
themes.angle: AI's North Star is no longer China, but American data-center politics.

themes.title: Markets discipline the AI-hardware trade
themes.summary: A renewed chip sell-off knocked South Korea's KOSPI lower, a Chinese humanoid robot maker leapt hundreds of percent on its Shanghai debut, and FT pushed back on superhuman humanoid valuations. Confidence is split between hardware euphoria and chip-capex jitters.
